text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:

- On Monday 18 members of the Slovenian parliament started a two-day visit to Brussels where they met representatives of the European Commission and NATO in order to debate Slovenia's prospective membership in the EU and NATO.

- Representatives of Slovenia, Austria and Italy met in Maribor on Monday to discuss preparation for stricter border controls that will be introduced from October in line with the EU's Schengen Agreement.
- About half of Slovenia's 31 political parties failed to present financial reports for 1996 to parliament and the Payment Agency by the end of March as required by law.

- The leftist United List of Social Democrats said it would on Friday stop collecting signatures of citizens that are in favour of a referendum which would limit the return of forests that were nationalised after World War Two to their previous owners.

- A group of Slovenian companies, including petrol trader OMV Istrabenz, said it would form a GSM company that would apply for a licence to operate a mobile telephone network. Currently, state-owned Mobitel is the only mobile telephone operator in the country.
- The Association of Free Slovenian Trade Unions said reforms to the pension system should not influence those that will retire in the next 10 years.
- Some 500 companies from 27 countries will be represented at a five-day construction fair in Gornja Radgona that will start on April 15.
